corrections.stars_or_usage: 108 stars, 15 forks, 3,808 commits; latest release v3.0.1 (2026-09-15)
corrections.caveats: Not an equal-precision comparison: the GMP/MPFR columns are 512-bit, the dd and qd columns are 106 and 212 bits, so the speedups mostly reflect hardware double arithmetic versus software bignum. The manual itself says the double results 'are not competitive to OpenBLAS or Intel MKL' (OpenBLAS DGEMM reached 1.46 TFlops on the same CPU). The author notes MPFR is about twice as slow as GMP, possibly because of copies in the MPFR C++ binding. First-party numbers from the arXiv user manual (version 2.0, 2022); the 2023-2026 releases (2.1.0 through 3.0.1, including a GMP/MPFR wrapper migration to gmpfrxx_mkII in 3.0.0) were not re-benchmarked in what was read. The 486,829 MFLOPS A100 figure is the kernel-only log (log.Rgemm.dd_cuda_kernel); the matching log including transfers (log.Rgemm.dd_cuda_total) peaks at 381,882 MFLOPS at n = 2296 (derived from page data). Benchmark optimization flags are not stated (manual examples use g++ -O2). last_commit is from the master commits page (2026-09-19, 'Fix commit-based QA source checkout').

notes: All manual figures (19/693, 11/390, 33/1300, 365/11200 MFlops) and the derived ratios check out; the A100 kernel log shows 486829.770 MFLOPS at n = 562. last_commit corrected from the topics-page 'updated' date (2026-09-30) to the latest master commit seen (2026-09-19).

tier_reason: First-party README tables only. The standalone benchmark (mr_blackwell.cu, 'make bench') times only the GPU kernel and prints its 'vs CPU' ratio by dividing by a hard-coded constant 13700; GMP (mpz_probab_prime_p) is called only as an untimed correctness check, so the 132x is not measured by the published harness. The only measured head-to-head is the first-party prime-gap pipeline table (28.0 s CPU vs 3.1 s GPU), without GMP version or CPU build flags.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README standalone table: v2d kernel 1,805,000 PRP/sec at 683 bits labelled 132x versus 'CPU (GMP) 13,700' on a Ryzen 9 8800X3D (as named in the README), and 295,000 PRP/sec = 21x at 1240 bits; but the benchmark program computes these ratios against a hard-coded 13,700 constant rather than timing GMP. Measured end to end in the prime-gap pipeline (P=503, 13K tests): CPU gap_test_simple 28.0 s versus GPU v2 3.1 s, about 9x (derived from page data), with kernel throughput about 1,800,000 versus 13,700 PRP/sec. CGBN on Blackwell is described as 'impractical' / 'orders of magnitude slower' with no numbers.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 3 stars, 1 fork, 18 commits; the README says it produced 60 prime-gap world records (as of 2026-05-05) through the sethtroisi/prime-gap pipeline
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers. The standalone benchmark's 'vs CPU' column divides by a hard-coded 13700 (printf '%.1fx vs CPU@13700' in mr_blackwell.cu); GMP is used there only as an untimed correctness check via mpz_probab_prime_p(n, 1), so the 132x/21x ratios are not reproduced by the published harness. The 13,700 PRP/sec figure comes from sethtroisi/prime-gap's gap_test_simple, whose main loop is single-threaded at HEAD (no OpenMP), so the ratio is a GPU against what appears to be one CPU core; GMP version and CPU build flags are not stated. 'Ryzen 9 8800X3D' is the README's name for the CPU and does not match a known AMD model name, possibly a typo. The source header says 5-bit window by default while the README says 4-bit. Only Blackwell (sm_120) is tested; other architectures are listed as 'should work (untested)'. The CGBN-on-Blackwell slowness claim is the author's own observation without numbers. last_commit 2026-05-05 confirmed on the master commits page.

notes: Downgraded because the headline 132x is a hard-coded denominator in the benchmark program (similar in kind to the zokio precedent, though here the constant matches a separately reported CPU pipeline run); the measured pipeline comparison gives about 9x end to end. Kept at C rather than rejected; orchestrator may record this as a 'baseline not measured by harness' shortcoming.
